note: A track whose first segment carries times and whose second does not, in the one arrangement that separates three readings instead of two. Moving time is unknown. Section 3.5 makes it derivable only when every segment carries a time on its first and last pip, because a sum over the segments that happen to be timed is indistinguishable from a complete one and no consumer can tell which it was given: zero at least reads as suspicious, a partial sum does not. Every other track in this corpus is wholly timed or wholly untimed, so nothing else here separates a reader that answers unknown from one that sums what it has. Three implementations summed, the reference one included, and every tier stayed green. The second segment's middle pip carries a time and its two end pips do not, and that is the whole reason the segment has three pips rather than two. It is what separates a reader that takes a segment's first and last pip, which section 3.5 requires, from one that reaches inward for the first and last timed pip. With both ends untimed and nothing between them, those two readings agree that the segment is untimed and the case passes either way. A file whose second segment carried no timed pip at all would therefore separate only two of the three readings, which is why the middle pip is here. Delete that middle pip, or give it no time, or give either end one, and the file goes on passing while testing one reading fewer. Red-proofed three ways. Summing the timed segments unconditionally reddens this case and two others, so that proof cannot say which rule it broke; summing them but still answering unknown when no segment is timed reddens this case alone; reaching inward for the first and last timed pip also reddens this case alone, and would return 60000 ms plus a zero-length span for the second segment.

tracks.name: Timed on the way up, not on the way down
